title: Alysis Code CLI to VS Code backend parity matrix
source_policy: Curated product policy validated against static extraction from Python CLI definitions, IDE bridge methods, VS Code package commands, and the extension slash registry.

policy_rationales.server_start_cli_only: server start stays CLI-only for now because lifecycle, authentication, and port exposure need a separate host policy instead of a VS Code command.
policy_rationales.terminal_menus_not_scraped: terminal-style config and setup menus must not be terminal-scraped; IDE support must be typed metadata or native VS Code UI.
policy_rationales.forge_swarm_blocked: forge swarm remains blocked until worker lifecycle, cancellation, sandbox, and approval UX are strong enough for parallel mutation.
policy_rationales.hooks_watch_blocked: hooks watch is a long-lived stream and should not be added as a simple request/response method.
policy_rationales.secrets_not_protocol_params: unsafe inline secret operations must not be added to protocol params; extension credentials and provider header values stay in VS Code SecretStorage, existing CLI config, or structured configure-provider flows.
policy_rationales.management_outputs_redacted_bounded: management responses and errors are centrally redacted; retained session logs and rendered conventions are bounded and include truncation metadata.
policy_rationales.update_check_passive_safe: update check defaults to cached/local status in IDE flows and performs network checks only after explicit user-triggered allow_network or force params.
policy_rationales.install_sources_validated: skill install and ext install validate source shape before invoking internals; local paths are workspace-scoped where allowed, remote sources require explicit policy, URL userinfo is rejected, and extension packages must be registry ids or pinned HTTPS git sources.
policy_rationales.forge_execute_v1_policy: IDE Forge Execute v1 is selected-task review mode only. The extension forwards explicit no_log and optional positive max_steps params, refreshes persisted plan artifacts/diffs after credential bridge restart, rejects subagents_enabled params while advertising subagents_supported=false, supports cooperative checkpoint cancellation for active selected-task jobs, and does not expose auto/fullaccess execution, swarm, or hard-interrupt cancellation.

aliases.rationale: `skill create` and `skill init` are Typer aliases decorating the same Python function and map to the same structured IDE method, `skill.init`.
`skill uninstall` and `skill remove` are Typer aliases decorating the same Python function and map to the same structured IDE method, `skill.remove`.

entries.rationale: Typer group namespaces are tracked so new groups cannot appear silently; concrete subcommands and IDE methods carry the actual parity decision.

entries.name: server
entries.rationale: The server namespace is intentionally CLI-only until lifecycle, authentication, and port exposure policy exists for IDE hosts.
These CLI workflows have typed VS Code command, Cockpit, slash, grouped backend-action, health, session, sandbox doctor, Forge, or management equivalents and do not require terminal-output scraping.

The broad CLI Forge exec command remains larger than IDE Forge Execute v1 review mode; IDE callers may pass explicit no_log and optional positive max_steps, but auto/fullaccess execution stays blocked until cancellation, sandbox, worker lifecycle, and approval guarantees are stronger.
entries.security_or_lifecycle_reason: Broad Forge exec can enter auto/fullaccess-style mutation and requires worker lifecycle ownership, stronger cancellation guarantees for broad mutation, sandbox guarantees, and approval UX before IDE exposure. VS Code exposes only typed selected-task review-mode execute aliases.

entries.rationale: forge resume continues an interrupted run by delegating to the sequential execution engine with retries enabled, so it inherits every constraint on broad CLI Forge execution. It also adds a decision of its own: when the plan drifted while the run was dead, --reapprove accepts work that was never approved. That approval belongs in typed IDE UI showing the drift, not in a terminal-scraped flag.
entries.security_or_lifecycle_reason: Resume performs broad plan mutation under the same worker-lifecycle, cancellation, sandbox, and approval gaps that block forge exec, and its --reapprove path grants execution approval for a plan the user has not reviewed in the IDE. The run state it reports on is already exposed: forge show/status carry run_status, run_status_reason, run_owner and resumable, and a crashed run reconciles to interrupted on read, so hosts can render an interrupted run truthfully without being able to resume it.

entries.rationale: forge unlock without --force only clears locks whose owner is provably gone, which is already automatic on acquisition and needs no IDE surface. The command exists for the ambiguous cases, and its one real power -- --force -- is what must not be a button until there is an approval surface for it.
entries.security_or_lifecycle_reason: --force clears a lock whose owner was not provably dead. If that process is alive, two executions can mutate the same workspace at once, so exposing it needs an explicit approval UX rather than a protocol method.

entries.rationale: These remaining provider authentication and long-running watcher operations need explicit Workspace Trust, typed lifecycle, cancellation/cleanup, bounded redacted events, and approved secret storage before IDE support.
entries.security_or_lifecycle_reason: Provider login needs flow-id persistence, an IDE-owned browser/device-code lifecycle, status polling, timeout/cancel cleanup, and an approved token-store write path. Provider logout needs a typed, confirmed credential-removal flow. hooks watch needs a subscription registry, bounded redacted event buffer, dropped-event accounting, watcher cancellation, and stop cleanup.

entries.name: mcp auth login
entries.rationale: The VS Code MCP Login action now routes through the complete typed lifecycle: Workspace-Trust-gated start, explicit HTTPS browser opening, durable flow status polling, cancellation, owned loopback callback cleanup, state + S256 PKCE, and encrypted token persistence. Codes and tokens never cross the IDE protocol.

entries.name: forge swarm
entries.rationale: Forge swarm is now a first-class IDE workflow: the cockpit Run Swarm console (renderSwarmConsole) and the alysis.runSwarm command dispatch the active plan across parallel workers behind the forgeSwarm capability gate and Workspace Trust. Workers run without --yes auto-approval (dangerous actions raise non-modal task-attributed approvals); merge is review-only (per-task Keep/Discard via forge.swarm.apply/discard, never auto-merged, untracked-files surfaced); cancellation is cooperative; failed/interrupted tasks offer an editable regenerate-subtree recovery. Terminal forge swarm keeps --yes and auto-merge.

These commands are terminal setup/maintenance, provider-account inspection, legacy asset migration, local sandbox image management, server startup, or secret mutation flows; they must not be terminal-scraped or accept unsafe inline secrets through IDE protocol params.
The Cockpit implements these as native slash routes, typed session/backend actions, settings/status UI, or help without forwarding unknown slash text to the model.

The VS Code extension exposes safe typed /trace and /terminals list/show/kill routes, but it does not expose arbitrary terminal creation, interactive PTY streaming, raw unredacted trace disclosure, or provider login/logout through untyped slash forwarding.
entries.security_or_lifecycle_reason: Provider login/logout needs an IDE-owned browser/device-code and credential-removal lifecycle with explicit confirmation. Terminal start/interactive streaming needs an IDE-owned subscription lifecycle, cancellation model, and approval UX; raw trace disclosure remains blocked because provider headers, environment values, and prompt-like content must stay backend-redacted and bounded.

entries.rationale: These terminal navigation, quick-panel, active-child picker, and toolbar affordances use native IDE surfaces. The IDE /subagents status|on|off route exposes typed delegation configuration; the CLI active-child monitor remains a terminal surface.
The extension exposes Forge help, plan display, and active-plan asset actions through typed Cockpit, Forge Plan, and backend-action routes.

The VS Code extension exposes typed Forge plan-edit routes for assistant instruction, goal updates, and task show/update via forge.plan.getState, forge.plan.setAssistant, forge.plan.setGoal, and forge.plan.updateTask. Mutations are Workspace Trust gated and use optimistic plan revisions instead of terminal Forge chat state.
Forge-context /plan inspection and regeneration use typed Forge methods. Chat plan mode and global /plan are retired; new IDE plans are explicitly created through /forge plan.

entries.name: /execute
entries.rationale: Terminal Forge /execute plan drives full-plan parallel mutation. The IDE now exposes that as the capability-gated Run Swarm console (forgeSwarm gate + Workspace Trust), with cooperative cancellation, the disjoint-write-scope scheduler invariant, the swarm-layer write guard, non-modal approvals replacing --yes, and review-only merge (per-task Keep/Discard, never auto-merged). It is experimental-with-gate rather than fully implemented because broad auto/fullaccess execution and merge-to-base stay blocked: the IDE swarm is review-only and selected by capability, not an unscoped chat command.
entries.security_or_lifecycle_reason: Broad auto/fullaccess Forge execution and direct merge-to-base remain blocked in the IDE; the swarm path is gated by the forgeSwarm capability, Workspace Trust, per-task approvals, and review-only apply/discard.

entries.rationale: These are terminal Forge mode navigation/finalization commands; the IDE uses persistent typed plan state and native view lifecycle.
These IDE Protocol v1 methods are documented, advertised by health.py, and consumed by VS Code feature gates, controllers, or typed bridge-client methods.

entries.name: host.action.respond
entries.rationale: The extension host uses this correlated response method only for capability-negotiated, workspace-fenced Tasks and Debug requests. Responses bind the exact request, session, workspace identity, fence, and serialized size limits; stale, duplicate, cancelled, late, untrusted, and unsupported requests fail closed.

Durable queue management, session search, external checkpoints, and explainable permission management are routed through bounded native BackendActionController workflows. Authority-changing actions retain Workspace Trust and explicit-confirmation gates; large results stay in the redacted Alysis Code output channel instead of crossing the webview boundary.

The native Browser Cockpit routes the complete lifecycle through a bounded typed controller. Public sessions are shared with the top-level agent; separately confirmed Direct IDE sessions permit only public and loopback destinations and are filtered and rejected by every model-controlled browser tool. Screenshots are verified, previewed through private webview URIs, and saved only through native Save As; snapshots and semantic diagnostics are bounded, redacted, and coalesced outside the chat stream.

Async job form of forge.plan.regenerate on the shared bridge job registry, mirroring forge.plan.start/forge.plan.result. The planner runs outside the bridge state lock (snapshot, compute, commit) with cooperative checkpoint cancellation via forge.cancel; the commit re-checks the persisted plan revision and fails closed with stale_plan_revision when a concurrent plan edit landed during regeneration. The typed bridge client covers both methods.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: Cockpit routes still call sync forge.plan.regenerate; the cockpit adopts the async pair in the Forge-swarm-in-IDE track before any user-facing route is added.

entries.rationale: Async job form of forge.review on the shared bridge job registry: the review provider call runs in a job thread instead of freezing the stdio dispatch loop, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints before and after the provider call and structured failure codes preserved. Sync forge.review remains for back-compat.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: Cockpit review routes still call sync forge.review; adoption of the async pair lands with the Forge-swarm-in-IDE cockpit work.

entries.rationale: The cockpit Run Swarm console (renderSwarmConsole + alysis.runSwarm) routes these typed bridge methods: forge.swarm.start creates an idempotent durable job and runs the swarm engine behind Workspace Trust with cooperative cancellation; the task grid renders swarm_worker_state_changed progress by glyph/weight; non-modal task-attributed approvals replace --yes (workers stay paused, never auto-denied); forge.swarm.review lists per-task diffs (with the untracked-files-not-applied list surfaced) which the user keeps via forge.swarm.apply (working tree only, never commits) or drops via forge.swarm.discard; failed/interrupted tasks offer an editable regenerate-subtree recovery.

The Forge Cockpit exposes a bounded durable recovery picker backed by workspace/session-scoped list and revision-fenced resume calls. Resume requires Workspace Trust and a fresh explicit confirmation, never reuses prior grants, cancels superseded local ownership safely, and keeps interrupted task worktrees isolated for review.

entries.name: forge.swarm.reconcile
entries.rationale: Post-crash/reload reconciliation: a read-only per-task report (merged / interrupted with diff-available / unstarted) over run artifacts and preserved worktrees, plus explicit idempotent harvest/discard actions. Typed-client covered (forgeSwarmReconcile) but not yet surfaced as a cockpit recovery flow β€” it backs harvest/discard and crash recovery beneath the Run Swarm console.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: The crash-recovery reconcile UX (a post-reload harvest/discard surface) lands as a follow-up; the method is typed-client covered and exercised by the swarm console's apply/discard paths but has no standalone user route yet.

entries.name: mcp.auth.login.start
entries.rationale: The bridge starts a durable, non-blocking OAuth flow with an owned one-shot loopback callback and returns only a flow id plus browser URL. The extension explicitly opens the HTTPS URL, polls status, and supports cancellation. State + S256 PKCE, encrypted token persistence, timeout cleanup, logout fencing, and shutdown cleanup are enforced without returning codes or tokens through protocol params.

The VS Code OAuth progress flow polls durable status and sends Workspace-Trust-gated cancellation. Both methods validate the configured workspace/server binding and return only allowlisted public flow state; listener credentials, completion leases, codes, and tokens remain backend-only.

The backend and typed VS Code bridge client cover exact-session MCP server status, enable, disable, and restart. Status is bounded and redacted; mutations require Workspace Trust and an idle owning session, while enable/restart atomically reject catalog drift instead of replacing a live server with incompatible tools, resources, or prompts.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: No standalone user-facing VS Code control is exposed yet. The typed, capability-negotiated client contract is ready for a separately reviewed native MCP lifecycle UX.

entries.name: bridge.shutdown
entries.rationale: The typed bridge client requests graceful shutdown before exact process-tree fallback. The backend cancels active work and closes sessions, OAuth listeners, managed runtimes, and owned resources within a bounded deadline.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: This is an internal lifecycle method rather than a user-visible backend action, command, or Cockpit control.

entries.rationale: The native review presenter starts and bounded-polls working-tree, branch/base, commit, and range reviews, then atomically projects workspace-contained, redacted, range-clamped findings into VS Code Problems. Starting, cancellation, failure, and replacement clear stale diagnostics, and controller disposal cancels active presentation work.
Durable session-scoped tasks use revision CAS and one active-task enforcement; structured questions use idempotency, expiry, crash recovery, fenced one-shot resolution, and bounded redacted payloads.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: The backend and typed client are complete; native task progress and question controls belong to the subsequent frontend wave.

entries.rationale: Hosts add a user message to the running turn through the same steering inbox the TUI uses; the turn reads it at its next step and logs steer_message_delivered with the text. chat.steer.take returns messages a finished turn did not read so the host can send them next. Refused without a running turn.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: The backend and typed client are complete; the Alysis Code desktop app is the first host to use them. A VS Code steering control belongs to a later frontend wave.

entries.name: forge.cancel
entries.rationale: The method is implemented as cooperative checkpoint cancellation for active Forge jobs, advertised through features.forge.cancel.supported, and routed by the VS Code Cancel Current Run command without relying on method presence alone.
entries.security_or_lifecycle_reason: Forge cancellation is cooperative, not a hard interrupt. Jobs enter cancellation_requested, stop at backend checkpoints or pending approval boundaries, emit bounded redacted events, and reconcile active_job/last_job before the UI reports a terminal cancelled state.

entries.name: features.forge.execute.unsafe_modes
entries.rationale: IDE protocol intentionally blocks auto/fullaccess Forge execution and exposes no experimental flag by default.
entries.security_or_lifecycle_reason: Auto/fullaccess modes need stronger cancellation guarantees for broad mutation, sandbox guarantees, approval routing, and worker lifecycle ownership before IDE exposure.

entries.name: features.run_chat_options.session_method_capabilities
entries.rationale: The bridge advertises explicit semantics for session.history, session.context, session.compact, session.resume, and session.images: history snippets are backend-redacted and bounded, context token counts are approximate tokenizer estimates or explicitly unavailable, compaction uses the live CLI conversation compactor when available, resume performs bounded redacted retained-session log replay without unbounded context summary insertion, and image baskets use workspace-scoped paths without JSONL binary transfer.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: This is capability metadata consumed by the extension to gate existing session routes; it is not a standalone user workflow.

entries.name: stdio-jsonl
entries.rationale: IDE Protocol v1 transport is newline-delimited JSON over stdio; the extension consumes this protocol and must not scrape terminal output.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: Transport selection is an internal extension/backend contract and is not exposed as a VS Code command, slash route, tree route, or Cockpit action.

entries.rationale: These command-palette entries are contributed by package.json and route to typed extension controllers or recovery helpers. alysis.locateCli locates, validates, and persists the Alysis Code CLI path safely.

entries.name: alysis.manage.refresh
entries.rationale: The Manage tree view-title refresh command is contributed by package.json, registered by manageCommands.ts, and refreshes the ManageViewProvider without hidden backend side effects.

These hidden Sessions tree context commands are contributed by package.json, hidden from the command palette, registered by sessionCommands.ts, and route explicit active/retained session rows through BackendActionController actions. Show, score, usage, and resume receive the selected tree session id; compact and clear remain active-live-session only.

These hidden Manage tree context commands are contributed by package.json, hidden from the command palette, registered by manageCommands.ts, and dispatch clicked domain rows to valid BackendActionMetadata actions. ManageViewProvider exposes context-menu tokens only when the exact backend action capability, selected item state, and Workspace Trust make the action reachable.

entries.name: alysis.manage.mcpLogin
entries.rationale: The hidden Manage tree MCP Login command is capability-gated on the complete start/status/cancel lifecycle and Workspace Trust. It opens only the bridge-provided HTTPS URL after confirmation and provides cancellable progress until the encrypted credential write reaches a terminal state.
The optional native VS Code chat participant is a thin router into the Cockpit and typed extension controllers.
These webview slash commands are registered in SlashCommandRegistry.ts and route through extension controllers, not terminal CLI parsing.

These aliases are registered in SlashCommandRegistry.ts and route only to the existing Forge Execute Review path. Broad execute arguments return a structured IDE v1 warning; auto/fullaccess execution remains blocked.

Persona listing and switching are consumed by the extension's persona picker, /persona slash command, and persona chip. The clamp rule keeps every switch non-escalating: a persona may lower the effective execution mode, never raise it.

entries.name: /ask
entries.rationale: The CLI runs one read-only turn and restores prior permissions. The IDE protocol has no per-turn permission override or restore handshake. The extension explains this limitation and offers the persistent Ask persona without pretending it is a one-turn equivalent.

entries.name: /chat
entries.rationale: The CLI retired /chat in favor of the Ask persona and one-turn /ask. The IDE likewise guides users to ordinary chat or /persona ask.
CLI provider model inventory and selection helpers. VS Code retains its existing typed provider/configuration controls rather than invoking these terminal commands.

entries.name: commands.list
entries.rationale: Read-only CLI slash command metadata for host-native composer menus.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: Consumed by the desktop composer. The VS Code typed client supports this query but its command menu has not adopted the shared catalog.

entries.rationale: Hosts build the same private report as the TUI's /report "Send to Alysis" (feedback_delivery): redacted description, engine version and, only when asked, OS, Python version and the last session messages. feedback.send sends exactly the reviewed bytes, tied to the Alysis account when signed in and anonymous otherwise; the report_id makes retries safe.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: The backend and typed client are complete; the Alysis Code desktop app is the first host to use them. A VS Code report control belongs to a later frontend wave.

entries.rationale: Machine-readable commands consumed by the Alysis Code desktop host or release validation. VS Code uses its existing typed IDE protocol and does not launch the desktop Host v2 lifecycle.
Capability-negotiated responses from the trusted Alysis Code desktop host for browser start, Computer Use and per-turn task budgets.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: The desktop owns these private media, approval and budget boundaries. VS Code does not negotiate or implement the desktop host capability; these methods are intentionally excluded from its typed client coverage, while bridge dispatch and protocol documentation remain required.

entries.rationale: Subagent model settings. Hosts read them with the agents.list bridge method; the desktop host saves with `agents set`, as it saves other settings with `config set`. VS Code has no subagent settings page yet.

entries.name: agents.list
entries.rationale: Read-only subagent and role model metadata for host settings pages: each subagent's model and provider as a run would resolve them, and why one is unavailable.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: Consumed by the desktop Settings. The VS Code typed client supports this query but has no subagent settings page.

entries.rationale: Host dispatch receipts and structured user questions are scoped to the active session and job.
entries.bridge_only_rationale: These negotiated host interfaces are available to desktop clients. The VS Code frontend does not yet implement the question or dispatch UI.

entries.name: profile check
entries.rationale: Validate a saved profile or a key read from stdin without changing stored credentials.
